entries.name: LiveScript
entries.definition: A functional-style programming language that compiles to JavaScript, descended from CoffeeScript.

entries.name: Logo
entries.definition: An educational programming language known for turtle graphics, developed in the 1960s by Wally Feurzeig, Seymour Papert and others.

entries.name: Lua
entries.definition: A lightweight, embeddable scripting language created at PUC-Rio in Brazil.

entries.name: Luxembourgish
entries.definition: A West Germanic language, a national language of Luxembourg.

entries.name: Macedonian
entries.definition: A South Slavic language, the official language of North Macedonia.

entries.name: Maithili
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken in the Mithila region of Bihar in India and in southeastern Nepal.

entries.name: Malagasy
entries.definition: An Austronesian language, the national language of Madagascar.

entries.name: Malayalam
entries.definition: A Dravidian language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Kerala.

entries.name: Maltese
entries.definition: A Semitic language with many Romance loanwords, the national language of Malta.

entries.name: Mandarin
entries.definition: The group of Chinese varieties spoken across northern and southwestern China, whose standard form is the official language of China.

entries.name: Manipuri
entries.definition: A Tibeto-Burman language of Manipur in northeastern India, also called Meitei.

entries.name: Manx
entries.definition: The Celtic language of the Isle of Man, a Goidelic language closely related to Irish and Scottish Gaelic.

entries.name: Marathi
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Maharashtra.

entries.name: MATLAB
entries.definition: A proprietary programming language and numeric computing environment from MathWorks, built around matrix operations.

entries.name: Mayan languages
entries.definition: A family of related languages spoken by Maya peoples in Mexico, Guatemala, Belize and Honduras.

entries.name: Media Center Markup Language
entries.definition: An XML-based markup language used to build user interfaces for Windows Media Center applications.

entries.name: Mizo
entries.definition: A Tibeto-Burman language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Mizoram.

entries.name: Mongolian
entries.definition: A Mongolic language, the official language of Mongolia.

entries.name: MQL4
entries.definition: A C-like programming language for writing indicators, scripts and automated trading programs on the MetaTrader 4 trading platform.

entries.name: MUMPS
entries.definition: A programming language with a built-in hierarchical database, developed at Massachusetts General Hospital in the 1960s and used in healthcare systems.
variants: Massachusetts General Hospital Utility Multi-Programming System

entries.name: MXML
entries.definition: An XML-based markup language created by Macromedia, later Adobe, for laying out user interfaces in Flex applications.

entries.name: Ndebele
entries.definition: The name of two related Bantu languages: Northern Ndebele, spoken mainly in Zimbabwe, and Southern Ndebele, spoken in South Africa.

entries.name: Nepali
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language that is the official language of Nepal and is also spoken in parts of India.

entries.name: Nim
entries.definition: A statically typed, compiled programming language with a Python-like syntax.

entries.name: Norwegian
entries.definition: A North Germanic language, the official language of Norway, written in the Bokmål and Nynorsk standards.

entries.name: Oberon
entries.definition: A programming language designed by Niklaus Wirth in the late 1980s as a successor to Modula-2.

entries.name: Objective-C
entries.definition: An object-oriented extension of C used for Apple's macOS and iOS software.

entries.name: OCaml
entries.definition: A general-purpose functional programming language of the ML family with an object system, developed at Inria.

entries.name: Odia
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Odisha.

entries.name: OpenEdge ABL
entries.definition: Progress Software's high-level, business-oriented programming language for the OpenEdge platform, formerly known as Progress 4GL.

entries.name: Ovambo
entries.definition: A Bantu language, also called Oshiwambo, spoken mainly in northern Namibia and southern Angola.

entries.name: Oz
entries.definition: A multiparadigm programming language supporting functional, logic, constraint and concurrent programming, implemented by the Mozart Programming System.

entries.name: Pascal
entries.definition: A structured, imperative programming language designed by Niklaus Wirth around 1970 and widely used for teaching programming.

entries.name: Pashto
entries.definition: An Eastern Iranian language spoken mainly in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

entries.name: Perl
entries.definition: A high-level, general-purpose scripting language known for text processing and regular expressions.

entries.name: Persian
entries.definition: An Iranian language, the official language of Iran, closely related to Dari and Tajik.

entries.name: Phoenician
entries.definition: An extinct Canaanite language of the ancient Phoenicians, written in the Phoenician alphabet.

entries.name: PHP
entries.definition: The PHP programming language.

entries.name: PHP 7
entries.definition: Version-specific PHP concept; not all versions of PHP.

entries.name: PL/I
entries.definition: A multi-purpose programming language developed by IBM in the 1960s for scientific, business and systems programming.
